html:
The Chelan are an Interior Salish people of Lake Chelan and the nearby stretch of the Columbia River in north central Washington. Their name is usually said to mean "deep water", for the long, deep lake.

They fished for salmon in the Columbia, hunted in the foothills of the Cascades, dug roots and spent winters in villages near the lake's outlet. Their close relatives and neighbours were the Methow, Wenatchi and Okanagan. Settlers took the lake country in the late 1800s, and today most Chelan descendants are members of the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, set up in 1872.
